- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:297-305 and 314-364 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: _load_trigger_page defaults has_more to False when the saved payload is a bare array rather than a dict with pagination metadata. A single bare-array page therefore produces triggers_complete: true, bypassing the incomplete-listing guard that load_trigger_pages is designed to enforce.
  WHY: In practice the API always returns a dict envelope with has_more/next_cursor/data fields, and the pickup saves the full response. The bare-array path is only reachable when _load_json_value resolves a raw JSON array — either from a test fixture or from the envelope scan hitting [ before {. Neither scenario occurs in normal pickup operation, so this is a defense-in-depth gap with no demonstrated runtime trigger. The existing test at line 884 exercises this path for load_triggers (single page), and load_trigger_pages inherits the same behavior from _load_trigger_page.

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py: `_load_trigger_page`, line 300; `load_trigger_pages`, lines 336 and 343–364 | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: A trigger page with no pagination metadata is treated as a complete listing. `_load_trigger_page` defaults missing `has_more` to `False`, and a non-empty single-page input therefore passes `load_trigger_pages` as complete.
  WHY: The loader accepts bare arrays as trigger input. If such an array is truncated at the pickup’s `limit: 100`, or a page lacks `has_more`, `decide` skips the incomplete-listing guard and can restart a checker whose pending trigger was omitted.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/claude_checker_restart.py: `_load_trigger_page` lines 297-305 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: A bare-array payload (which the function explicitly accepts at line 303: `routines = payload.get("data") if isinstance(payload, dict) else payload`) defaults `has_more` to `False` at line 300. `load_trigger_pages` then treats that page as a complete listing. If a bare array happens to contain exactly 100 items (the `limit: 100` page size), `scan` reports `triggers_complete: true` and `decide` skips the incomplete-list guard, potentially restarting a checker whose pending trigger was omitted from the truncated page.
  WHY: The documented caller (the pickup) always passes the structured `{data, has_more, next_cursor}` format from the MCP tool, so this path is not exercised in normal operation. But the function explicitly accepts bare arrays as a supported input shape (the ValueError check at line 304 validates them), so a truncated bare array — from a manual export, an older tool version, or a format change — would silently bypass the fail-safe the cursor-chain validation was added to provide. The fix is one line: when `payload` is not a dict, set `has_more = True` so the listing is treated as incomplete.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- Note on the pass-1 gpt-6-luna finding: it claims a bare-array / metadata-less trigger page is treated as complete because `_load_trigger_page` defaults `has_more` to `False`. This is pre-existing behavior of the original `load_triggers` (the single-page path the pickup used before this PR), and `load_trigger_pages([page])` is explicitly asserted to equal `load_triggers(page)` in the new test. The real `list_triggers` API response is always an object carrying `has_more` and `next_cursor`; a bare array is only reachable via a direct Python call, never from the pickup path the diff changes. Truncation-without-`has_more` is a theoretical precondition not evidenced in the changed code or its callers, so it falls under the anti-rule on theoretical risks and was not promoted.

The cursor-chain validation in `load_trigger_pages` (scripts/claude_checker_restart.py:328-369) correctly catches an omitted intermediate page: the page after the gap is read with the missing page's `next_cursor`, which the `cursors[index] != next_cursor` check compares against the prior page's cursor. The count-mismatch, empty-paths, last-page-still-`has_more`, and early-termination-of-non-last-page cases are all handled and asserted by the new tests (`test_trigger_pages_join_and_take_has_more_from_the_last_page`, `test_trigger_pages_with_a_page_left_out_between_two_others_are_incomplete`, and the two end-to-end CLI tests). The pickup command file at the current head carries the cursor-passing instructions the test asserts, consistent with the twin-sync commit dd77257.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
